title.value: Negotiate a lower Comcast bill via chatbot

introduction.value: DoNotPay's ChatGPT-based bot chatted with Comcast support for an engineer and secured a $10 monthly discount.

method.value: DoNotPay built a bot on the OpenAI GPT-3 API that chats with company support. An engineer typed a request to lower the internet bill while keeping the same plan. The bot waited through Comcast's automated chat until a live agent joined. It then sent a long message claiming outages, lost work and a threat to leave, and exchanged pleasantries.

outcome.value: It secured a $10 monthly discount, about $120 a year. The bot invented the outages, left a placeholder like [insert email address] in its text, and was too polite. Part of the chat was with Comcast's own bot.

notes.value: The bot fabricated the outage claims, which Browder called a liability problem. The public version was meant to cite laws and threaten to leave without making things up.

introduction.en: A DoNotPay demonstration used an OpenAI-powered bot for an internet-service retention conversation.
introduction.zh: DoNotPay 的演示使用基于 OpenAI 的机器人与网络服务商讨论留客优惠。

method.en: DoNotPay built the negotiation bot using OpenAI’s GPT-3 API. An engineer requested a lower internet bill while keeping the existing service plan.
method.zh: DoNotPay用OpenAI GPT-3 API构建议价机器人，工程师要求保持原套餐并降低网络账单。

method.en: The bot waited through automated Comcast support until a person joined, then negotiated using complaints about outages and lost work and a threat to leave.
method.zh: 机器人等待Comcast自动客服转接人工，再以断网、工作损失及转投他家的说法议价。

outcome.en: The claimed concession was $10 each month, equivalent to $120 over a full year. Some of the conversation was bot-to-bot; it is not evidence of cash already received.
outcome.zh: 声称获得每月10美元优惠，完整一年对应120美元；部分交流发生在机器人之间，不能作为已收到现金的证据。

notes.en: The outage complaints were invented, an email placeholder remained in a message, and the tone was excessively polite. The source identifies fabricated claims as a liability concern; actual ChatGPT/GPT-based tooling differs from the suggested Operator template.
notes.zh: 断网投诉是编造的，邮件占位符未替换且语气过度客气；源站指出虚构诉求的责任问题，实际GPT工具也不同于模板推荐的Operator。

What they did

The bot waited through Comcast's automated chat until a live agent joined. It then sent a long message claiming outages, lost work and a threat to leave, and exchanged pleasantries.
How it went
It secured a $10 monthly discount, about $120 a year. The bot invented the outages, left a placeholder like [insert email address] in its text, and was too polite. Part of the chat was with Comcast's own bot.
Worth knowing
The bot fabricated the outage claims, which Browder called a liability problem. The public version was meant to cite laws and threaten to leave without making things up.

with

Copy prompt
Open the online support chat for [provider, e.g. internet or phone company] and ask for a lower monthly bill on my [plan name], where I currently pay [amount]. Mention [loyalty length, competitor offer or promo] and ask about discounts. Do not accept any new terms or contract changes; pause and show me any offer in writing before I decide. Finish by summarizing what was offered.
